text:
elena_ops: oncall created a war room for a customer-facing spike — multiple customers seeing 502/504 + timeouts on hosted inference in eu-west, some mentions of "auth failed" in logs. creating thread, cc @miguel_sre @ash_support :warning:

oncall-bot: Incident 1715432100 — hosted-inference eu-west partial degrad, severity P1 (auto-detected). Joining: @miguel_sre, @ravi_runtime.

miguel_sre: looking at gateway metrics now, p50->p95 latency jump around 11:12 UTC, concurrent 502s from ingress -> 5xx from auth-proxy and backend timeouts. correlating with deploy?

ash_support: customers piling up tickets, one attached logs showing "401 token verification failed" and then a stream of 504s. attaching excerpt from CorpApp: 
```
{"error":"auth token verify timeout","trace":"auth-proxy::verify:timeout"}
```

priya_ingest: I'm seeing a small burst of billing/KMS latencies at the same time window — KMS US->EU cross-region call had retry backlog. Could be auth token validation blocked waiting on KMS.

ravi_runtime: if auth checks block, requests sit in gateway and can trigger downstream timeout/fallbacks — we had a similar auth-cache storm in Q1. adding kv-cache and auth-proxy logs.

miguel_sre: quick checks: 1) rollback the auth-proxy canary? 2) increase auth-proxy timeouts to avoid tx pile-up? 3) enable degraded-mode that bypasses KMS for cached tokens? thoughts.

elena_ops: customer impact high, prefer mitigation first (increase timeouts + fallback to cached tokens) then root cause. please coordinate comms with support.

ash_support: I'll send an ack to customers and let them know we're mitigating, ETA 15m.

ravi_runtime: rolling a config change to auth-proxy: `AUTH_VERIFY_TIMEOUT=5s -> 10s`, and enabling `AUTH_BYPASS_CACHE=true` for requests with valid stale cache. applying to eu-west canary now.

miguel_sre: canary shows drop in 502s after 60s, backend queue length down 40%. pushing to remainder of fleet.

priya_ingest: KMS team confirmed a transient spike due to key rotation job that caused a small latency bump — they paused rotations. adding KMS throttle guard to prevent cross-region fanout.

elena_ops: action items from war room: 1) rollback risky canary (we didn't deploy new code) — we changed timeouts and enabled bypass (owner: ravi_runtime, done) 2) KMS rotation guard + alert (owner: priya_ingest, in progress) 3) add auth-proxy circuit-breaker to avoid head-of-line blocking (owner: miguel_sre) 4) support comms + postmortem (owner: ash_support)

miguel_sre: short-term mitigations applied. for postmortem: need traces showing request path where KMS call latency->auth verify -> gateway queueing -> 5xx. capture p95 token-verify duration per region and correlation with 5xx spikes.

ash_support: customers updated, one wants SLA credit check, logged to billing-escalations.

elena_ops: good. let's meet in 24h for postmortem draft. closing war room but keeping thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident 1715432100 status -> mitigated.

miguel_sre: preliminary note for postmortem: root cause = KMS rotation job causing elevated key service latency -> auth-proxy token verification timeouts -> gateway queueing -> client-facing 502/504s. Contributing: no circuit breaker on auth-proxy, timeouts conservative for catastrophic KMS latency, no KMS rotation guard.

ravi_runtime: repro steps captured: 1) simulate KMS latency (200ms->1s) for token verification 2) send steady stream of requests with short TTL tokens 3) observe gateway queue growth -> 504s. attaching synthetic harness in internal repo.

priya_ingest: remediation plan (short/long): short = KMS rotation pause + throttles, auth-proxy timeout increase and bypass; long = circuit breaker, per-region KMS caching, rotation staging, alert on KMS tail-latency.

ash_support: assigned postmortem doc to support template: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/1715432100 (will populate).

elena_ops: thanks team. keeping open for final artifacts.

miguel_sre: final ask: add test to CI that injects KMS latency and validates gateway SLOs won't catastrophically degrade (owner: eng-sre).

ash_support: noted. closing for now, will re-open if customers report recurrence. :pray:
